name: AKU Conference on Postgraduate Medical Education

content.text: Professor Roger A. L. Sutton, Dean, Faculty of Health Sciences, AKU, welcomed the guests and highlighted the necessity for developing strong postgraduate programs to impact the health needs of Pakistan. AKU has graduated 241 clinical generalists and specialists from its 24 postgraduate programs since 1991, many of whom are now working at AKU and as faculty and staff at other teaching institutions in the country.

Professor Farhat Moazam, Associate Dean of PGME at AKU, noted in her presentation that educators must recognize the imbalance that exists between the service and educational components of most training programs in the country. She said that"postgraduate programs, by labeling their residents as 'trainees' tend to primarily focus on acquisition of technical skills. As a result, the equally important attributes that must be inculcated in physicians, such as ethical behavior, a compassionate approach, professionalism and communication skills, are often ignored." Recognizing this deficiency, AKU has introduced a mandatory core curriculum for residents, which addresses these aspects of resident education.

The first session of the conference dealt with the experiences of other specialized centers of excellence in Pakistan, involved in providing care to the ill in specific areas. This included a presentation by Professor Adibul Hasan Rizvi, Director, Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation (SlUT), about the struggles and achievements of SlUT. Dr Yusuf Kamal Mirza, CEO of the Shaukat Khanum Memorial Cancer Hospital, also gave an outline of the inception and mission of that institution. Dr Ashfaq Ali Khan, Director Training, Marie Adelaide Leprosy Center, spoke about the successful fight against leprosy in Pakistan, and AKU's role in helping them achieve this goal.

The plenary session devoted to postgraduate medical education began with an overview of the problems and challenges of postgraduate training in Pakistan, presented by Professor Naeem A. Jafarey, Vice Chancellor of Ziauddin Medical University. He was followed by Professor Rosslynne Freeman from the University of London, who elaborated on the changing culture of postgraduate medical education and how it must serve as a force for change. The trend is for educators to move from an authoritarian mode of teaching to one that is facilitatory and interactive. Professor Renee Fox from the University of Pennsylvania spoke on bioethics as a component of medical education, and the difficulties inherent in applying a western, secular model of ethics in societies where codes of ethic are family centered and based on religious values.

Dr Qasim Mehdi, Director General, Biomedical and Genetic Engineering Division, Dr A. Q. Khan Research Laboratory, focused on the discovery in his laboratory of novel genes in inherited eye diseases, and the international reputation that young Pakistani researchers have acquired in this field. He believed that with the will, right support and resources, researchers in this country could be second to none in the world. Professor Sarwar Zuberi, Scientist Emeritus, Pakistan Medical Research Council (PMRC) and Dean for Research at Ziauddin Medical University, then enumerated the hurdles that the PMRC continues to face in promoting medical research.

content.title: AKU Conference on Postgraduate Medical Education
content.author: Ambreen Nadeem
content.description: The Department of Postgraduate Medical Education (PGME) of the Aga Khan University (AKU), organized a conference on "Healthcare: Keeping Pace with New Challenges." The conference covered several areas of importance to both young physicians and those involved in their training. It included a series of lectures by national and international speakers and workshops for residents in patient consultation skills and data analysis.
